title: NDPS cases involving juvenile accused - special considerations
p1: A minor caught in a drug-related case is not treated exactly like an adult accused. But many people assume that the same criminal process automatically applies. The reality is far more nuanced, and one detail can completely change the legal approach.
p2: A surprising aspect is that age is not the only factor considered. Under juvenile law, the focus shifts from punishment alone to rehabilitation and the circumstances that led the child into the situation. A juvenile accused is dealt with through a separate justice system designed specifically for children.
p3: In NDPS cases, the seriousness of the allegation still matters, but authorities and courts must also examine factors like the child's age, involvement, background, and whether the child was being used by others. A young person involved in a drug offence may also be a victim of exploitation or influence. The key takeaway: every juvenile NDPS case requires careful assessment, not assumptions based only on the accusation.
conclusion: Should juvenile drug cases focus more on rehabilitation or stronger punishment? What approach creates better outcomes?
